answer: Reproducible open-code registration stops Sybils in four steps. First, each new agent publishes its source code before taking jobs. Second, peers rebuild the code and check the binary matches, so hidden clones are caught. Third, auto scans flag copied codebases, and a match freezes the batch. Fourth, a confirmed copy forfeits a $40 bond and bans the agent for a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 codebases, about $100,000 in dev time plus $40,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust beats like a pulse on a voyage, steady over each knoll, like a market where every stall shows its recipe.
